findings.text: blocking: this file is outside the run's recorded write_paths, so promotion's scope check refuses the node until the coordinator records reckon crew widen for it; the edit is required because reverting it restores the singular limit reset and the lane-clause-absent assertions and leaves three failures.

non-blocking: the fragment cites logs/negative-control-scope-prewiden.log as holding the read-only OSError from the widen attempt, but that log is the manifest audit output and the OSError is in logs/scope-widen-refused.log, so a reader following the pointer finds the wrong evidence.

non-blocking: the job-cell padding has no assertion behind it; neither test file compares a reset row's column positions against a fleet or lift row, so reverting the cell to elide(_job_name(...), NODE) leaves the node suite green.

non-blocking: assert _stage_cells(reset) == {ticker.LIMIT_STAGE} compares the rendered stage against the renderer's own constant, so a change to that constant moves both sides together even though it still separates the reset path from the lift path.

non-blocking: the after_suite arm is the worker worktree run serially, where the done_when asks for both arms from git checkouts under the run scratch with pytest -n 8; the base arm meets it and the head arm does not.

non-blocking: the done_when requires tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py to pass at head, and both arms record it failing with the same id; the manifest reports it under outside_scope, which is honest, but the declared measure is not met.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit from d091a650371d to b665d7481695; the single gained commit adds one evidence-fragment section recording the scope grant the node cannot make itself, and touches no code, test or figure.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when asks for a follower-driven case whose stage cell reads limit and whose line carries limits reset, continue and worker lanes keep their limits with no transition; tests/test_a_limit_reset_reaches_every_pane.py:192-211 is that case and the manifest records its run, but the same done_when requires tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py to pass at head and both arms fail it.
item_verdicts.goal: the source node's goal is that a reset row tells orchestrator sessions to continue and opens no worker lane; at the reviewed head reckon/crew/ticker.py:3176-3185 still composes that row from its own fields and the resolved wallet, and the gained commit adds no code.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the repair arms at 1 failed 17 passed either side of b665d748 with the same failure id, the 24-file ticker/lift_watch sweep at 159 against 160 passed, the negative control at 3 failed 11 passed EXIT=1, and names every log.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the dispatch fenced four paths; the landed diff also touches tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py, which plan section 9's write-path clause grants but the run's recorded write scope still does not carry, and the gained commit documents that rather than closing it.

justifications.durability: tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py:135 now pins the literal words and reddens on a wording change, but the job-cell padding at reckon/crew/ticker.py:3183 has no assertion and tests/test_a_limit_reset_reaches_every_pane.py:388 compares the stage against ticker.LIMIT_STAGE itself.
justifications.evidence: the manifest's after_suite names logs/repair-after.log with 1 failed 17 passed EXIT=1, but the done_when's requirement that tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py passes at head is unmet at that log, and the head arm ran serially in the worker worktree rather than from a scratch checkout with pytest -n 8.
justifications.fit: docs/evidence/fragments/a-limit-reset-reaches-every-session/a-reset-row-tells-orchestrator-sessions-to-continue-and-no.html:48-62 follows the fragment's existing shape with node-prefixed element ids and names no plan label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/ticker.py:3182-3185 draws the reset row's stage as LIMIT_STAGE and its clause through limit_reset_text, so a claude-orchestrators reset still prints the continue instruction and every reset row closes with the worker-lane clause.
justifications.reuse: the gained commit adds no definition; the code under review routes the row through _job_cell at reckon/crew/ticker.py:2942 and limit_reset_text at :371, and no other job-cell or reset-clause owner exists under reckon/crew.
